To ensure they captured the authentic movements of their rodent cast, the Pixar animation team kept several enclosures of pet rats in the hallways of their studio for over a year. The animators spent countless hours observing the animals to understand the exact mechanics of their fur, the rapid twitching of their noses, and how their skeletal structure allowed them to compress their bodies to squeeze through tight spaces.
However, director Brad Bird made one crucial, character-defining deviation from real rat anatomy specifically for the protagonist. While the rest of the rat colony scampers around normally on all fours, Remy almost exclusively walks upright on his hind legs. This was a deliberate, subtle design choice to emphasize his passion for the culinary arts—Remy considers himself a true chef, and he absolutely refuses to let his front paws touch the dirty ground before he handles food.

Ratatouille (2007), directed by Brad Bird, starring Patton Oswalt, Ian Holm, Lou Romano, Janeane Garofalo, Peter O’Toole. A highly ambitious rat with an extraordinary sense of taste and smell forms an incredibly unlikely, secret alliance with a clumsy kitchen worker to achieve his dream of becoming a renowned chef at a prestigious fine-dining restaurant in Paris.
